label: Shipping / Logistics
description: Templates, glossary terms, and examples for freight, dispatch, warehouse, and customer shipment updates.

templates.label: Shipment update
templates.body: Start with the shipment status, then note location, next milestone, ETA or ETD, and any blocker. Keep it concise and customer-friendly.

templates.label: Delay notification
templates.body: State the delay clearly, explain the operational reason without over-speculating, give the updated ETA when available, and close with the next step or follow-up time.

templates.label: Operations handoff
templates.body: Use short bullets for issue, current status, next action, owner, and timing. Prefer operational shorthand over prose.

templates.label: Incident summary
templates.body: Summarize the exception, the impact, what has already been checked, and the next action. Keep it direct and structured.

examples.label: Delay notification example
examples.output: Shipment update: the container is running behind the original ETA due to port congestion. The revised ETA is tomorrow evening. We are monitoring the vessel closely and will send the next update once discharge is confirmed.

examples.label: Operations note example
examples.output:
- Shipment held at customs for document review
- Broker requested corrected BOL reference
- Ops team sent updated paperwork

styles.customer_voice: clear and reassuring without sounding defensive
